narrative: Special Note: Calves weaned longer than 45 days are left untagged. Compared to last week: Yearling steers and heifers were both too lightly tested to develop any market trend. Steer calves under 350 lbs were too lightly tested to develop an accurate market trend, however higher to sharply higher undertones were noticed. 350-449 lbs steers sold mostly 15.00-20.00 higher; 450-499 lbs sold mostly steady to 8.00 higher; 500-699 lbs steers sold fully steady; steers over 700 lbs not well compared. Heifer calves under 400 lbs were too lightly tested to develop an accurate market trend, however steady to higher undertones were noticed. 400-449 lbs heifers sold 15.00-20.00 higher, 450-649 lbs heifers sold mostly 5.00 higher, heifers over 650 lbs were not well compared. Quality this week was mixed, but mostly average to attractive. Many cutback cattle were seen off summer videos this sale. Some of these cattle looked stale after last weeks rain and snow storm and were discounted as a result. Canadian buyers all struggled with trucking logistics this week as many report trucking is very tight. Several buyers filled loads and exited the market early which led to wide price spreads again this week. Light weight steers and heifers destined for western grass sold on very good demand this week. Buyers have started CME positions were mostly steady this week. The October contract closed Friday at 343.625, 0.225 lower than last Fridays close. The November contact close Friday at 341.90, 0.05 lower than last Fridays close. The January contract closed at 338.275, 1.925 higher than last Fridays close. Market activity was mostly active with a moderate crowd of buyers noticed at all feeder specials. Weigh up cows sold on mostly moderate demand for moderate offerings. Demand for feeding cows was stronger again this week as American packers and Canadian feeders both showed good demand for high quality cows to feed. Private feeders were active again this week as well. Many private feeders were willing to take lame or blemished cows to feed. Feeding cows sold mostly 5.00 higher on breaking cows, boning and lean cows sold steady to 2.00 higher. A large pool of feeding cow buyers was seen this week. Slaughter cows sold on light demand this week. The quality and yield of cows destined for immediate harvest is very low as feeding buyers continue to buy cows away from packers. Breaking cows sold steady to 2.00 higher, boning cows sold fully steady and lean cows sold steady to 2.00 lower on a lower yielding offering. Slaughter bulls sold 3.00-4.00 higher on a slightly higher yielding offering. Bulls have started to regain some condition lost during breeding season as late fall rains have greened pasture and range conditions. Yields have improved as a result. Young age offerings sold on good to very good demand. Young age offerings sold mostly steady on like quality offerings. Quality this week was not as attractive as last weeks offering.
